drinks.title: Bloody Mary
drinks.history: Fernand Petiot claimed to have first mixed vodka with tinned tomato juice at Harry's New York Bar in Paris around 1921, then refined it with spice and lemon at the St. Regis in New York in the 1930s. The hotel thought the name too coarse and sold it as a Red Snapper for years.
steps: Add plenty of ice to a shaker along with two parts vodka, four parts tomato juice, half a part of fresh lemon juice, four dashes of Worcestershire sauce, four dashes of Tabasco, and a sprinkle of salt and pepper. Tilt the shaker back and forth before shaking vigorously. Strain into a tall glass and garnish with a celery stick.
notes: Petiot's first version was a plain half-and-half of vodka and tomato juice; the seasoning came later in New York. A saviour for fragile mornings.

drinks.title: Breakfast in Bed
drinks.history: A house cocktail from Elephant Rock's own menu, described there as "bright, fragrant, zesty" — lemon-infused gin lengthened with a black tea syrup, in the mould of a gin fizz. The menu lists the ingredients but not the measures, so the proportions below are a standard bartender's estimate.
steps: Shake lemon-infused Boatyard gin, black tea syrup and lemon juice hard with plenty of ice in a cocktail shaker, then strain into a chilled coupe glass or over fresh ice in a rocks glass. Garnish with a lemon twist.
notes: Bright, fragrant and zesty, per the bar's own menu — a good one for someone who wants a G&T with a bit more going on.

drinks.title: Candy on the Coast
drinks.history: A house cocktail from Elephant Rock's own menu, described there as "velvety, creamy, sweet" — raspberry-infused vodka and Amarula with strawberry and a candy floss syrup, finished with cream. The menu lists the ingredients but not the measures, so the proportions below are a standard bartender's estimate.
steps: Shake raspberry-infused vodka, Amarula, strawberry syrup, candy floss syrup and cream hard with plenty of ice in a cocktail shaker, then strain into a chilled coupe glass. Garnish with a swirl of candy floss if you have it.
notes: Velvety, creamy and sweet, per the bar's own menu — a genuine dessert cocktail, best treated as one.

drinks.title: Drunk Elephant
drinks.history: A house cocktail from Elephant Rock's own menu, described there as "nutty, dense, sweet" — cold brew and cacao playing off the toffee-nut warmth of Amarula and Frangelico, with cacao bitters to round it off. The menu prints the ingredients but not the exact measures, so the proportions below are a standard bartender's estimate rather than the bar's own recipe card.
steps: Shake Amarula, Frangelico, cold brew coffee, crème de cacao and cacao bitters hard with plenty of ice in a cocktail shaker, then strain into a chilled coupe glass. Garnish with a light grating of cacao or a coffee bean.
notes: Nutty, dense and sweet, closer to a boozy dessert than a bright cocktail — a good one to finish a meal on rather than start with.

drinks.title: Elephant 75
drinks.history: A house cocktail from Elephant Rock's own menu, described there as "sweet, tart, dry" — a French 75 built on Copeland Rhuberry gin with a dash of Cointreau added, topped with prosecco. The menu lists the ingredients but not the measures, so the proportions below are a standard bartender's estimate.
steps: Shake Copeland Rhuberry gin, Cointreau, lemon juice and sugar syrup hard with plenty of ice in a cocktail shaker, then strain into a chilled Champagne flute. Top with prosecco. Garnish with a lemon twist.
notes: Sweet, tart and dry, per the bar's own menu — the rhubarb gin gives it a pink blush and a fruitier edge than a standard French 75.

drinks.title: Espresso Martini
drinks.history: Dick Bradsell made it at the Soho Brasserie for a model who asked for something that would, in her words, wake her up and then mess her up. He called it a Vodka Espresso first, then the Pharmaceutical Stimulant; the martini name came later and stuck.
steps: Combine vodka, cooled espresso, coffee liqueur, and plenty of ice into a cocktail shaker and rigorously shake until the outside of the shaker is cold. Strain into a chilled martini glass and garnish with three coffee beans.
notes: A stove-top coffee maker or even canned espresso work just as well if you don't have a coffee machine. Kahlua is the coffee liqueur of choice.

drinks.title: Hazelnut Old Fashioned
drinks.history: A house cocktail from Elephant Rock's own menu, described there as "nutty, rich, sweet" — an Old Fashioned built on Buffalo Trace bourbon with crème de cacao and hazelnut standing in for the usual sugar, plus cacao bitters. The menu lists the ingredients but not the measures, so the proportions below are a standard bartender's estimate.
steps: Stir Buffalo Trace bourbon, crème de cacao, hazelnut liqueur and cacao bitters with plenty of ice in a mixing glass until well chilled, then strain into a rocks glass over a large ice cube. Garnish with an orange twist.
notes: Nutty, rich and sweet, per the bar's own menu — a dessert-leaning Old Fashioned, closer to a boozy Nutella than the classic bitters-and-sugar version.

drinks.title: Margarita
drinks.place: Mexico and the US border — disputed
drinks.history: At least three people have claimed it: Carlos "Danny" Herrera at Rancho La Gloria near Tijuana around 1938, Dallas socialite Margarita Sames in Acapulco in 1948, and a Juárez bartender called Danny Negrete. The dullest explanation is probably the true one — margarita is Spanish for daisy, and a Daisy is simply a spirit, citrus and orange liqueur, which is exactly what this is. The first printed recipe ran in Esquire in December 1953.
steps: Prepare the glass by wiping the rim with lime and then placing it upside down on a bed of salt so that the rim has a light covering all the way round.
Shake tequila, triple sec, fresh lime juice and plenty of ice hard in a shaker, then strain into the glass over fresh ice. Garnish with a lime wheel.
notes: Many people's fear of tequila quickly dissipates when combined with that sweet double combo of lime juice and triple sec.

drinks.title: Mixed Berry Smash
drinks.history: A house mocktail from Elephant Rock's own menu — raspberry, blackberry and blueberry muddled with lime and sugar, lengthened with soda water, in the same smash format as a whiskey smash. The menu lists the ingredients but not the measures, so the proportions below are a standard bartender's estimate.
steps: Muddle a handful of raspberries, blackberries and blueberries with a sugar and lime juice in the base of a highball glass until the berries break down. Fill with ice and top with soda water. Stir gently and garnish with extra berries and a lime wheel.
notes: As fruity and full of pulp as a smash should be — leave the muddled berries in the glass rather than straining them out.

drinks.title: Mulled Cider
drinks.history: The cider-country cousin of mulled wine, from the orchards of the West Country. It shares its ancestry with wassail, the spiced-cider ritual of drinking to the health of the apple trees in midwinter.
steps: Combine the dry cider or fresh apple juice, apples, cinnamon sticks, allspice berries, orange zest, and dark rum (optional) in a large saucepan and simmer gently for 30 minutes - do not boil.
Transfer to a heatproof bowl and ladle into glass mugs. Garnish with apple to serve.
notes: Clove-studded apples, spices, citrus and dark rum make this mulled cider recipe impossible to resist on a cold day; a great Christmas party drink.

drinks.title: My Cherry Amore
drinks.history: A house cocktail from Elephant Rock's own menu, described there as "bold, warming, smooth" — a Manhattan built on cherry-infused Buffalo Trace bourbon and Carpano Antica Formula sweet vermouth, with bitters. The menu lists the ingredients but not the measures, so the proportions below are a standard bartender's estimate.
steps: Stir cherry-infused Buffalo Trace bourbon, Antica Formula sweet vermouth and angostura bitters with plenty of ice in a mixing glass until well chilled, then strain into a chilled coupe glass. Garnish with a cherry.
notes: Bold, warming and smooth, per the bar's own menu — a Manhattan for someone who wants the cherry garnish built straight into the spirit rather than left floating on top.

drinks.title: Negroni
drinks.history: Count Camillo Negroni is said to have asked barman Fosco Scarselli at Caffè Casoni to stiffen his Americano with gin in place of the soda. Family records suggest the Count had spent years in America as a gambler and rodeo rider before returning to Florence, which is the sort of detail that makes the story worth believing.
steps: Combine one part gin, one part sweet vermouth, and one part Campari into a mixing glass with ice and stir until the glass begins to feel chilled. Strain into a tumbler over fresh ice and garnish with a slither of orange peel.
notes: A perfectly balanced cocktail beloved by barmen worldwide. Although simple, always opt for the best quality spirits and aim for a sphere of ice rather than cubes.

drinks.title: Ode to Violet
drinks.history: A house cocktail from Elephant Rock's own menu — one of the bar's own bartender recommendations, described there as "floral, niche". Built like an Aviation with a double measure of gin and an egg white for body, it leans further into the crème de violette than most, letting the perfume lead. The menu lists the ingredients but not the measures, so the proportions below are a standard bartender's estimate.
steps: Dry shake Boatyard double gin, crème de violette, St Germain elderflower liqueur, lemon juice and egg white without ice first to build the foam, then shake again hard with plenty of ice in a cocktail shaker. Strain into a chilled coupe glass.
notes: Floral and a little niche, as the bar's own menu puts it — closer to a perfume counter than a fruit bowl. Worth trying before dismissing the violette as too much; the lemon and gin keep it from tipping into potpourri.

drinks.title: Old Fashioned
drinks.history: A cocktail was defined in print in 1806 as spirits, sugar, water and bitters — nothing more. By the 1880s bartenders were mixing fancier things, so drinkers who wanted the original started asking for it the old-fashioned way, and the name stuck to the drink. The Pendennis Club in Louisville claims to have made it famous.
steps: Add a teaspoon of caster sugar to a rocks glass with a few splashes of Angostura Bitters and a splash of hot water or soda water to dissolve the sugar. Stir until all of the sugar has dissolved and add a few ice cubes and one part whisky. Stir for 1 minute before topping up with ice and an orange peel or slice to garnish.
notes: Works well with both bourbon and scotch. The bitters and sugar are there to round out the spirit, not hide it.

drinks.title: Pear & Elderflower Spritz
drinks.history: A house spritz from Elephant Rock's own menu, described there as "fruity, light, crisp" — Poire Williams pear brandy and St Germain elderflower liqueur lengthened with prosecco, in the same built-over-ice, topped-last format as an Aperol Spritz. The menu lists the ingredients but not the measures, so the proportions below are a standard bartender's estimate.
steps: Fill a large wine glass with ice, then add Poire Williams and St Germain elderflower liqueur and stir briefly. Top with prosecco, poured gently so it doesn't lose its fizz. Garnish with a thin pear slice.
notes: Fruity, light and crisp, as the bar's own menu puts it — an easy-drinking spritz for anyone who finds Aperol too bitter.

drinks.title: Pear Shaped
drinks.history: A house mocktail from Elephant Rock's own menu — apple juice, pear purée, lime juice and passionfruit shaken together, no spirit at all. The menu lists the ingredients but not the measures, so the proportions below are a standard bartender's estimate.
steps: Shake apple juice, pear purée, lime juice and the pulp of passionfruit hard with plenty of ice in a cocktail shaker, then strain into a highball glass over fresh ice. Garnish with a thin pear slice.
notes: Named for the pun as much as the pear — a fruity, fully non-alcoholic option that doesn't taste like an afterthought.

drinks.title: Storehouse Martini
drinks.history: A house cocktail from Elephant Rock's own menu, described there as "rich, bold, creamy" — an espresso martini built on vanilla vodka and Kahlúa, deepened with a Guinness and demerara sugar reduction in place of a plain sugar syrup. The name nods to the stout. The menu lists the ingredients but not the measures, so the proportions below are a standard bartender's estimate.
steps: Shake vanilla vodka, Kahlúa, cooled espresso and Guinness and demerara reduction hard with plenty of ice in a cocktail shaker for a good foam, then strain into a chilled martini glass. Garnish with three coffee beans.
notes: Rich, bold and creamy, per the bar's own menu — a stout-and-coffee twist on the espresso martini rather than a straight copy of it.
The Guinness and demerara reduction is simmered stout reduced down with demerara sugar until syrupy; make a batch and it keeps in the fridge for other coffee drinks too.

drinks.title: Swamp Juice
steps: Put the leaves of the fresh mint into a pestle and mortar with a pinch of white sugar and bruise it down (don't liquidise). Rinse the pestle and mortar out with a bit of vodka into a large bowl.
Add all the lime juice and pulp into the bowl too, along with the rest of the vodka, the white rum, and the runny honey.
Stir it up so the honey gets mixed in and allow it to marinade in the fridge for a day if possible, or minutes if you can't.
Take a large highball glass (holding at least 350ml), fill it with whole and half-crushed ice, then half fill with the boozy mixture and top off with ginger beer.
Drink. Share. Fall over. Repeat.
notes: Full name is Dr Lucy Darawallahs Swamp Fever, named after a doctor in Nairobi who inspired the vodka honey bit, a character in a John Irving novel (misspelled), and an 11 yr old niece who introduced some of the chaos that resulted in the elixir itself. For sweetness, start off with slightly less honey the first time and see if that's sweet enough; you can always add more later. If you hate ginger beer, try tonic instead.

drinks.title: The Aul Lammas Fair
drinks.history: A house cocktail from Elephant Rock's own menu, described there as "sweet, citrus, balanced" and named for Ballycastle's Auld Lammas Fair — Ireland's oldest traditional fair, held every August since the 17th century, famous above all for yellowman, the hard golden honeycomb toffee sold from its stalls (as the old ballad goes: "Did you treat your Mary Ann / to some Dulse and Yellow Man / at the Ould Lammas Fair in Ballycastle-O"). The drink's nod to it is YellaMan, an actual honeycomb vodka liqueur made by Niche Drinks in nearby Derry/Londonderry, lengthened here with Cointreau, marmalade, lime and lemonade. The menu lists the ingredients but not the measures, so the proportions below are a standard bartender's estimate — and since YellaMan is a liqueur rather than a plain vodka, it's already sweetened, so this needs less added sugar than a typical vodka sour.
steps: Shake YellaMan honeycomb vodka liqueur, Cointreau, a marmalade and lime juice hard with ice in a cocktail shaker, then strain into a highball glass over fresh ice. Top with lemonade. Garnish with a lime wheel.
notes: Sweet, citrus and balanced, per the bar's own menu — the YellaMan liqueur is what makes this one, giving it a honeycomb sweetness no ordinary vodka sour has. If you can't get hold of it, a plain vodka with a splash of extra honey syrup is the closest substitute.

drinks.title: The Sweet Talker
drinks.history: A house cocktail from Elephant Rock's own menu, described there as "nostalgic, sweet" — bon-bon-infused vodka lengthened with blood orange tonic, built long over ice. The menu lists the ingredients but not the measures, so the proportions below are a standard bartender's estimate.
steps: Fill a highball glass with ice, add bon-bon-infused vodka, lemon juice and a sugar and stir briefly. Top with blood orange tonic. Garnish with a lemon wheel.
notes: Nostalgic and sweet, per the bar's own menu — built for anyone who wants their vodka to taste like a sweet shop.

drinks.title: Virgin Bramble
drinks.history: A house mocktail from Elephant Rock's own menu — the bar's alcohol-free take on a Bramble, built on Tanqueray 0.0% alcohol-free gin with grenadine and lime in place of the usual gin and crème de mûre. The menu lists the ingredients but not the measures, so the proportions below are a standard bartender's estimate.
steps: Fill a rocks glass with crushed ice, add Tanqueray 0.0%, lime juice and sugar syrup and stir briefly. Drizzle grenadine over the top of the crushed ice last, unstirred, so it bleeds down through the glass. Garnish with a blackberry and a lime wedge.
notes: The drizzle is what makes a Bramble a Bramble, alcohol-free or not — pour the grenadine over crushed ice last and leave it alone rather than stirring it in.

drinks.title: Virgin Pornstar Martini
drinks.history: A house mocktail from Elephant Rock's own menu — the bar's alcohol-free take on a Pornstar Martini, built on passionfruit purée, lime and sugar syrup lengthened with pineapple juice instead of vanilla vodka and Passoã. The menu lists the ingredients but not the measures, so the proportions below are a standard bartender's estimate.
steps: Shake the pulp of passionfruit, lime juice, sugar syrup and pineapple juice hard with plenty of ice in a cocktail shaker, then strain into a chilled coupe glass. Garnish with half a passionfruit balanced on the rim.
notes: Traditionally served with a shot of prosecco alongside — swap it for a splash of soda water or sparkling grape juice to keep this one fully alcohol-free.

drinks.title: Virgin Strawberry Daiquiri
drinks.history: A house mocktail from Elephant Rock's own menu — the bar's alcohol-free take on a frozen strawberry daiquiri, built on strawberries, lime, sugar syrup and grenadine with no rum. The menu lists the ingredients but not the measures, so the proportions below are a standard bartender's estimate.
steps: Blend strawberries, lime juice, sugar syrup, grenadine and a scoop of ice until smooth, then pour into a chilled coupe glass. Garnish with a strawberry slit onto the rim.
notes: Blend it thick — the point of a frozen daiquiri, alcohol-free or not, is a proper slush rather than a thin smoothie.
